issue.title: floor() function doesn't work in v0.0.73

repository.name: promxy
repository.description: An aggregating proxy to enable HA prometheus

issue.body:
We updated Promxy from v0.0.72 to v0.0.73 and noticed that the values returned by the `floor` function are very far off from where they were before the update.

We tested by going back to v0.0.72 and then v0.0.73 to confirm that this is a problem with the latest release. We tested directly against prometheus and did not see this issue. Also, removing the floor aggregation shows the same results between v0.0.72 and v0.0.73, so it seems to be an issue with the aggregator specifically (though there might be additional aggregators that have problems).

Example (results are truncated for brevity):

Test expression:
```
curl -vk http://localhost:8082/api/v1/query_range --data-urlencode 'query=floor(CapacityRemainingMemory{placement_tag=~".+"} / (4*1024))' --data-urlencode 'start=1634677080' --data-urlencode 'end=1634677380' --data-urlencode 'step=15'
```

v0.0.72
```
{"status": "success", "data": {"resultType": "matrix", "result": [{"metric": {"ip": "10.0.4.20", "unit": "MiB"}, "values": [[1634677080, "3"], [1634677095, "3"], [1634677110, "3"]]}]}}
```

v0.0.73
```
{"status": "success", "data": {"resultType": "matrix", "result": [{"metric": {"ip": "10.0.4.20", "unit": "MiB"}, "values": [[1634677080, "3508224"], [1634677095, "3508224"], [1634677110, "3508224"]]}]}}
```

Any idea what could have caused this issue in the latest release?

body: @codesome  Is StepInvariantExpr meant to be printed at all? I expect that the parser generates expressions that can be printed, not so much the engine.

the query is parsed correctly, the parens are dropped as part of preprocessing and is expected (note, this does not change the query result)

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/c2d1c858577cdac009162d095ec80402b049949c/promql/engine.go#L2544-L2545
Here is the place where we remove the ParenExpr: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/c2d1c858577cdac009162d095ec80402b049949c/promql/engine.go#L2557

> not so much the engine

+1. prometheus currently [changes](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/6627) the AST while evaluation.
 
@jacksontj your test case is expected to fail due to 🔝 Also, the OP [mentions](https://github.com/jacksontj/promxy/issues/469)
>We tested directly against prometheus and did not see this issue. 

can you reproduce the incorrect query result in prometheus?

> @codesome Is StepInvariantExpr meant to be printed at all?

As you mentioned, it is only used during query execution. The only place it would potentially print it is any error messages that the engine produces.

> When parsed and printed I expected to see the same string

@jacksontj can you please elaborate on this point? Parse and print where/how

Another thing is that the `PreprocessExpr` method which adds the `StepInvariantExpr` is public. So we could try to fix this printing since it should be an equivalent query but with some wrapping here and there.
~A simpler solution is to treat `StepInvariantExpr` as a paren expr, hence add the parens when printing even when there is no paren while keeping the query semantics same.~ Fixing the root of this specific issue seems like a good idea, Julien has pointed out the exact code here https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/9591#issuecomment-951663510

@codesome Thanks for the input; my issue here is effectively what you describe (PreprocessExpr returns a non-equivalent query). Based on your input here it sounds like you guys are okay with removing the unwrapping -- so I've updated my PR to include that.
